# cardano-blueprint ledger conformance vectors

<!-- Generated by ledger-conformance BlueprintVectorGateTest (./gradlew :ledger-conformance:conformanceReport). Do not edit by hand. -->

ADR-056 §8 and Phase 7b. The Java engine (`java-engine`: rule `LEDGER`, origin `SYNC`, Scalus phase 2) replays every transaction of the cardano-blueprint ledger conformance vectors, Conway runs of the Haskell ledger's Imp tests.

- **Vectors**: cardano-blueprint PR #71 (`KtorZ/cardano-blueprint` at `d57b8d765395e54645824b6718b02c6565bc0ffc`), `src/ledger/conformance-test-vectors/vectors.tar.gz`, sha256 `5041539c9e2908cc897512f249ea16ec26bbb04cb1ec288dc59f47024a9b727d`; the same files as Amaru's `crates/amaru-ledger/tests/data/rules-conformance` at tag `v10.11.20260925` (corpus digest `39bf59ed66e31d7e61f7f9c41e924905d0795c0ae4324590d3a6bfe072a05ed2`). cardano-blueprint `main` (`0f0c17e1`) still carries the older JSON, one-transaction-per-file tarball, which is a different format. The extracted vectors are vendored under `ledger-conformance/vectors/cardano-blueprint` (its README has the pin and how to update it), so the gate does not depend on PR #71's fork commit staying available.
- **Format**: `[config, initial NewEpochState, final NewEpochState, [event], title]`, event `[0, tx, success, slot]` / `[1, slots]` (PassTick) / `[2, epochs]` (PassEpoch). A vector records whether Haskell applied each transaction, not the predicate failure.
- **Harness**: the initial state is decoded into an `InMemoryLedgerView` (`NewEpochStateDecoder`, fail closed); transactions run at their slot, the epoch under the vector's fixed epoch size, the state's protocol version, the vector's network id and system start, and no forecast horizon (the Imp tests' epoch info is fixed). Between transactions the state follows Haskell: an applied transaction's effects go into an `OverlayLedgerView` (the engine's, or `TxEffectsDeriver`'s for Haskell's verdict when the engine disagrees). **Tick and epoch events are skipped**, as in Amaru: a disagreement in a transaction whose epoch is later than the initial state's (`nesEL`) is `requires epoch`, not a failure. The boundary is taken from the state's epoch, not from the events: one dump records a PassEpoch its initial state already includes.
- **Final-state check**: for a vector that stays in one epoch with unchanged parameters, the state reached is compared with the vector's final `NewEpochState` (UTxO, accounts, pools, DReps, committee, proposals): it checks the effects the Java side derives. It is not full-state equality: votes, proposal payloads beyond type and parent, anchors, pool parameter bodies beyond deposit, VRF key and retirement, deposit/fee/donation totals, the stake distribution and snapshots are not compared (the rules do not read them); the treasury, enacted roots and dormant-epoch count are not compared because only an epoch boundary changes them.

## Final-state check

| Outcome | Vectors |
|---|---:|
| matched | 233 |
| not applicable: crosses an epoch boundary | 80 |
| not applicable: protocol parameters changed outside the events | 7 |

An Imp test can change the state without an event (`modifyPParams`): in the vectors listed as "protocol parameters changed outside the events" the final parameters differ from the initial ones although no epoch passed, so their transactions were validated against the initial parameters: `alonzo/fail-utxos-no-cost-model/0` (passed; java rejects [tx 2 with `UTXOW.PPViewHashesDontMatch`]), `alonzo/fail-utxos-plutusv2-no-cost-model/0` (passed; java rejects [tx 2 with `UTXOW.PPViewHashesDontMatch`]), `alonzo/fail-utxos-plutusv3-no-cost-model/0` (passed; java rejects [tx 2 with `UTXOW.PPViewHashesDontMatch`]), `conway/pass-enact-futurepparams/0` (passed; java rejects []), `conway/pass-ratify-a-parent-parameterchange-proposal-can-prevent-its-child-from-being-enacted/0` (passed; java rejects []), `conway/pass-ratify-other-lineage/0` (passed; java rejects []), `conway/pass-ratify-same-lineage/0` (passed; java rejects []). In the three `no-cost-model` vectors the verdict matches for another reason: the failing transaction was built against parameters without the script's cost model. `BlueprintVectorGateTest` validates the failing transaction of the three `no-cost-model` vectors against their final state, whose parameters hold no cost model at all: the Java engine reports Haskell's `UTXOS.CollectErrors [NoCostModel]` and nothing else, so the script integrity hash matches and `PPViewHashesDontMatch` is an artefact of the missing event. (Before Phase 7b, `ScriptIntegrity.costModel` read the empty cost-model map as unavailable and failed closed with `ENGINE.LedgerStateUnavailable`; an empty raw map now means "no cost model for any language", and only a `null` one, or an empty one beside a non-empty named map, is unavailable.)

## Decoder coverage

Initial states decoded: 320 of 320; final states: 320 of 320. Parts populated (vectors whose initial / final state has entries):

| Part | initial | final |
|---|---:|---:|
| accounts | 0 | 181 |
| committee hot keys and resignations | 0 | 72 |
| committee members | 320 | 320 |
| dormant epochs | 1 | 15 |
| dreps | 0 | 89 |
| enacted roots | 0 | 31 |
| future pool params | 0 | 1 |
| future protocol parameters | 1 | 81 |
| guardrail script | 320 | 319 |
| pools | 0 | 72 |
| proposals | 0 | 113 |
| retiring pools | 0 | 2 |
| treasury | 0 | 73 |
| utxo | 320 | 320 |

Not read (skipped by item boundaries): blocks made, snapshots, the reward pulser, the pool distribution, the DRep pulser, genesis delegations, MIR pots, deposits/fees/donation totals. The vectors use the CBOR `TxIn`/`TxOut` encoding for the UTxO and the `UMap` account layout; a MemPack-encoded UTxO or the later `PState` layout would fail closed. Rounded rationals (read only by the epoch boundary): [pvtHardForkInitiation = 2/3 rounded (read only by the epoch boundary), dvtHardForkInitiation = 2/3 rounded (read only by the epoch boundary)].
